By land, sea, air, Trump supporters vow massive statewide rally Sunday

By Wendy Rhodes

@WendyRhodesFL

Posted Jun 9, 2020 at 4:28 PM

From Pensacola to Miami, Tampa to West Palm Beach, Trump supporters say they will celebrate the president’s birthday and Flag Day with massive rallies and voter registration effort.

Frustrated by what they say is inaction by Republican Party of Florida, so-called “Trumplicans” say they plan to celebrate Flag Day and President Donald Trump’s birthday Sunday with large rallies across the state.

Organized by Trump Team 2020 Florida — an organization that lists more than 20 chapters and about 10,000 members statewide — the events are part of a larger effort to register voters to support the president’s re-election bid this November. It is something the group said the Florida Republican Party is not doing enough of.

In Palm Beach County, trucks will meet at 10 a.m. at Pirate’s Well Restaurant & Bar, 9477 Alt A1A in Lake Park. The route will be south of Interstate 95 to Southern Boulevard, and then back up the highway to the restaurant for an after party.

Motorcyclists will meet at the Cracker Barrel at 7461 SW Lost River Road in Stuart, and follow the trucks down Interstate 95 to Southern Boulevard, and then end at the Harley-Davidson store at 2955 45th Street in West Palm Beach for the after party.

Related content

Trump rally organizer: Police to provide security amid threats

June 11, 2020

Boats will take off from the Square Grouper Tiki Bar at the Jupiter Inlet, head down the Intracoastal Waterway to the Southern Boulevard Bridge and then head back the same rout for the after party. Last month, a “Trumptilla” support flotilla drew hundreds of others for a similar effort.

“If we don’t win Florida, we lose the election,” said Annie Marie Delgado, founder of Trump Team 2020 Florida. “The way Florida goes, the nation goes.”

The events, which are free and open to the public, are part of an all-out push by Trump Team 2020 Florida to register new voters, particularly veterans, Delgado said. That Sunday is also Trump’s birthday and Flag Day, she said, will only add to the excitement and camaraderie of the rallies.

“People are fed up with people destroying property, people tearing down our cities,” she said of the recent George Floyd protests. “They are fed up with being locked in their homes. They want out; they want freedom. And the American flag on Flag Day represents freedom.”

“After parties,” as she calls them, will take place in seven counties throughout the state and include birthday cake, music and speakers. Attendees can even sign one of a dozen 2-foot-by-1.5-foot birthday cards that will be sent to the White House.

Other Florida cities will also host “Trumptillas” — large parades of boats decked out in red, white and blue Trump gear. The Villages, a retirement community outside of Orlando, will host a golf cart parade, and motorcycles and trucks will make their way from city to city statewide to show their enthusiasm for the president. And to document the enormity of the event, professionally-piloted drones will capture it all on video, Delgado said.

“Trump Team 2020 Florida wants everyone to know that these rallies across the state of Florida are positive rallies,” she said. “We are not protesting anything or anyone, but we are in full support of our men and women in blue.”

Delgado founded Trump Team 2020 Florida out of frustration that the state GOP officials were not doing enough to get out the vote, she said. In fact, she is so disillusioned with the state party, she and her followers do not even call themselves Republicans, preferring instead the term “Trumplican.”

No one, she said, is more dedicated to Trump’s re-election than her organization, which she said has grown by leaps and bounds because people yearn to be active on a grassroots level and her group provides that opportunity.

Delgado said she hopes Trump recognizes the hard work and dedication of Trump Team 2020 Florida volunteers, who she said are dedicating their time and money to his re-election campaign with no financial support from the Republican Party.

“I would like to see the president’s campaign help us with funding for our voter registration and our outreach that we have been doing all on our own and our dimes,” she said of what she hopes will be one outcome of this event. “We’re running out of dimes.”

But the most important message Delgado said she hopes resonates with Trump is the need to pass laws to prevent voter fraud.

“One thing we want him to do is to communicate with Gov. DeSantis the importance of establishing an executing order for ballot harvesting,” she said. “If we don’t get that under wraps, we will lose Florida.”

Delgado said she encourages anyone thinking about attending one of the many rallies this weekend to check them out. She said it is a great way to meet like-minded individuals and show the president how much his work is appreciated, particularly in the shadow of the riots surrounding the George Floyd protests.

“We are going to unite and show support for this nation, this flag, our president, and everyone who has suffered the loss of their businesses that have been burned down to the ground,” she said.
